incidents.name: Loss of the Harker Vale
incidents.summary: Bulk carrier Harker Vale broke apart during an improperly documented ore-loading operation after departing a Carver habitat.
incidents.cause: Progressive structural overload caused by cargo distribution outside certified limits; investigation also found falsified loading records.
incidents.consequence: Modern Carver bulk terminals adopted independent mass verification. 'Harkering it' remains dock slang for pretending a load problem will fix itself.
incidents.tone: Industrial disaster caused by ordinary commercial pressure, not mystery.

incidents.name: Dock 14 Pressure Accident
incidents.summary: A docking adapter interpreted an obsolete pressure-ready signal as authorization to cycle a transfer collar.
incidents.cause: Standards translation failure between legacy hardware and modern port control.
incidents.consequence: Mandatory physical interlock revisions spread through Concord-standard docking equipment.
incidents.tone: Frequently taught in commercial certification courses.

incidents.name: Pelagos Storm Lift
incidents.summary: Six cargo craft and dozens of surface vessels coordinated evacuation and supply during a severe volcanic-island storm sequence.
incidents.consequence: Mixed orbital/surface logistics procedures developed afterward became standard across Pelagos.
incidents.tone: Remembered as an example of freight crews becoming emergency infrastructure.

incidents.name: Meridian Black Week
incidents.summary: A cascading power-distribution failure left large sections of Port Meridian on local backup for six days.
incidents.cause: Deferred replacement of original depot-era distribution equipment hidden behind decades of expansion.
incidents.consequence: Massive rebuild created today's segmented station grid. Old Ring businesses still display blackout lanterns during the anniversary.

incidents.name: The Three Pumps Run
incidents.summary: Independent freighter Three Pumps carried replacement atmosphere equipment to Waystation after two scheduled carriers declined a poorly insured emergency charter.
incidents.cause: A contaminant damaged habitat circulation machinery.
incidents.consequence: The ship's name became shorthand for small operators taking work large networks cannot price neatly.
incidents.tone: Famous without being heroic mythology; the crew was paid and argued about the rate afterward.

incidents.name: Talos First Winter Shortage
incidents.summary: Population growth outran storage and surface transport during Talos's first major winter after the mineral rush.
incidents.cause: Poor forecasting, weather and too much inbound construction cargo occupying warehouse capacity.
incidents.consequence: Food, heaters and water equipment commanded extreme emergency rates; new freight rules reserve storage for essential supplies.
incidents.tone: Recent event still shaping local attitudes.

incidents.name: Accord Overdue
incidents.summary: Survey vessel Accord failed to return from a cataloged target beyond Redoubt. No confirmed wreckage or distress transmission has been recovered.
incidents.consequence: Lastlight Survey Office tightened route-plan and reserve recommendations. The crew is listed overdue rather than legally presumed lost.
incidents.tone: A reminder that exploration can simply fail without revealing a conspiracy.
